title: ‘पिँधको मान्छे’ कवितामा सीमान्तीय अभिव्यक्ति {A marginal expression in the poem 'Pindhko Manche'}
nepali: प्रस्तुत अनुसन्धानमूलक लेख ‘पिँधको मान्छे’ कविताको विश्लेषणमा आधारित छ । प्रस्तुत कविता कवि गिरि श्रीस मगरद्वारा लिखित ‘एकलव्यको देब्रे हात’ कवितासङ्ग्रहमा समाविष्ट छ । उनी आफ्ना कवितामा विभिन्न कारणले पछाडि परेको वर्ग, समुदाय वा हेपिएको, अपमानित भएको, शोषित र दमित वर्गका कथाव्यथालाई अभिव्यञ्जित गर्न रुचाउँछन् । प्रस्तुत कविताले युगौँदेखि श्रमशोषणमा परेका र कहिल्यै माथि उठ्न नपाए÷नसकेका वर्गको विषयलाई उठाएको छ । ती वर्गका पसिनाको शोषण गरी सदैव उनीहरूमाथि शासन गर्ने माथिल्लो वर्गको शैलीप्रति कविताले व्यङ्ग्य गर्दै शोषितप्रति सहानुभूतिको भाव प्रकट गरेको छ । यस प्रकारको विषयवस्तुलाई सबाल्टर्न भनिन्छ भने साहित्यमा अभिव्यक्त सबाल्टर्नको अध्ययन गर्ने सिद्धान्तलाई सबाल्टर्न वा सीमान्तीय समालोचना भनिन्छ । प्रस्तुत समालोचनात्मक लेखमा ‘पिँधको मान्छे’ कवितालाई विश्लेष्य सामग्रीका रूपमा चयन गरी उत्तरआधुनिक समालोचनाका क्षेत्रमा विशेष महत्त्वको मानिने सीमान्तीय समालोचना सिद्धान्तका सापेक्षतामा अध्ययन–विश्लेषण गरी प्रस्तुत कविताले उठाएको सीमान्तीकृत वर्गको विषयलाई पहिचान गरिएको छ । युगौँदेखि सामन्तबाट शोषणमा परेका तर तिनको बारेमा कुनै पनि पक्षले नबोलेर मौन बसेकाले उनीहरू आफ्नो हकहितका पक्षमा आवाज उठाउन अक्षम रहेको सन्दर्भलाई नै कविताले अभिव्यक्त गरेको कुराको प्रकटीकरण गर्नु नै प्रस्तुत कविताको उद्देश्य रहेको निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ । कवितामा आर्थिक र चेतनाका दृष्टिले सीमान्तवर्गमा परेकाका करुणाजन्य अवस्थाको चित्रण गरेर तिनप्रति माथिल्लो वर्गको शून्य सहानुभूतिको व्यवहारका कारण सीमान्त वर्ग सदैव दमित अपहेलित रहन बाध्य रहेको भाव कवितामा व्यक्त भएको निष्कर्ष यस समालोचनात्मक लेखमा निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: The present research article is based on the analysis of the poem 'Pindhko Manche'. The present poem is included in the poetry collection 'Eklavyako Debre Haat' written by poet Giri Shrees Magar. In his poems he likes to express the tales of woe of classes and communities left behind for various reasons, or of those humiliated, insulted, exploited and oppressed. The present poem raises the issue of classes that have been subjected to labor exploitation for ages and have never been able to rise up. By satirizing the style of the upper class that always exploits the sweat of those classes and rules over them, the poem expresses a feeling of sympathy towards the exploited. This kind of subject matter is called subaltern, and the theory that studies the subaltern expressed in literature is called subaltern or marginal criticism. In the present critical article, selecting the poem 'Pindhko Manche' as the material for analysis, the issue of the marginalized class raised by the poem has been identified by studying and analyzing it in relation to the theory of marginal criticism, considered of special importance in the field of postmodern criticism. Since they have been exploited by feudal lords for ages but remained silent because no party spoke on their behalf, they were unable to raise their voice in favor of their own rights and interests, and expressing this very matter is the purpose of the present poem, this conclusion has been drawn. The conclusion drawn in this critical article is that, by depicting the pitiable condition of those fallen into the marginal class economically and in terms of consciousness, the poem expresses the sentiment that the marginal class is always forced to remain oppressed and despised because of the upper class's zero sympathy towards them.

informal_english: This research piece is all about analysing the poem 'Pindhko Manche'. The poem sits in the collection 'Eklavyako Debre Haat' by poet Giri Shrees Magar. He likes, in his poems, to give voice to the hard-luck stories of classes and communities left behind for all sorts of reasons, or of folk who've been humiliated, insulted, exploited and oppressed. The poem raises the issue of classes that have been worked to the bone for ages and never got the chance to rise up. By taking the mickey out of the upper class that always exploits their sweat and rules over them, the poem shows sympathy for the exploited. This kind of subject matter is called subaltern, and the theory that studies the subaltern in literature is called subaltern or marginal criticism. In this critical article, taking 'Pindhko Manche' as the material for analysis, the issue of the marginalised class raised by the poem has been picked out by studying it alongside the theory of marginal criticism, which carries special weight in postmodern criticism. Since they've been exploited by feudal lords for ages but stayed mum because nobody spoke up for them, they were unable to raise their voice for their own rights and interests, and expressing just that is the poem's purpose, that's the conclusion drawn. The conclusion here is that, by showing the pitiable state of those pushed into the marginal class economically and in awareness, the poem expresses the feeling that the marginal class is always forced to stay oppressed and despised because the upper class has zero sympathy for them.
